Art. 340: the President appoints a commission on socially and educationally backward classes (APP).
Outcome: First - Kaka Kalelkar Not implemented (UPSC); Second - B.P. Mandal 27% quota; implemented by V.P. Singh Govt in 1990; 27% of central civil posts reserved in 1993 (UPSC, IYB)
The Constitution does not define "backward classes" (G2 2017 key: that was the incorrect statement). Art. 16(4) backward classes are mainly identified by caste/social backwardness (Indra Sawhney).

Before 2018, Art. 338(10) treated references to SCs as including such backward classes as the President specified - hence BC complaints went to the SC commission ; the 102nd Amendment added Art. 366(26C) defining SEBCs by reference to Art. 342A .

Project Cheetah (17 Sep 2022) was the world's first intercontinental large-carnivore translocation. Kuno NP (MP) got 8 cheetahs from Namibia in 2022 and 12 from South Africa in Feb 2023. Gandhi Sagar WLS is the 2nd home and Veerangana Durgavati TR the 3rd. Population: 53 (APPCA 2026).

Great Indian Bustard (Rajasthan, Gujarat; fewer than 150 birds): the SC's 2021 order to put power lines underground was modified in 2024. Lines now go underground in priority habitats, with bird diverters elsewhere. The case is M.K. Ranjitsinh v. UoI (CDI calls it "Wildlife First v. UoI"). An SC expert panel proposed power corridors (LENS, Aug 2025). The first artificial-insemination breeding was at Jaisalmer…

bullets: Qubit can be 0, 1 or any state between (superposition); entanglement links qubits regardless of distance; decoherence (loss of quantum state through the environment) is the main barrier (TH, 9 Jul 2026).
Entanglement sudden death = abrupt total loss of entanglement; Raman Research Institute showed one well-timed local "quantum flip" can delay or prevent it (LENS daily, 16 Sep 2026).
DST quantum-safe report: post-quantum cryptography migration for Critical Information Infrastructure by 2029, others by 2033 (LENS daily, 31 May 2026).

Supremacy machines: Google Sycamore (2019) ; China's photonic Jiuzhang (2020) . Micius (China, 2016) = first quantum communication satellite . Microsoft's Majorana 2 chip raised qubit stability to 20-60 s (APPCA, 2026).
2025 = International Year of Quantum Science and Technology (UN; centenary of quantum mechanics) ; World Quantum Day = 14 April.

items.title: India’s First 5.56 km Free‑Space Quantum Key Distribution Link Demonstrated
items.summary: 03 OCT 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi QNu Labs, in collaboration with Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo‑informatics (BISAG‑N) and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated India’s first free‑space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link at a scale of 5.56 km.

facts.text: 03 OCT 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi QNu Labs, in collaboration with Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo‑informatics (BISAG‑N) and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated India’s first free‑space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link at a scale of 5.56 km.
Sunil Gupta, Co‑founder and CEO, QNu Labs, emphasized that the successful 5.56 km demonstration paves the way for longer‑distance quantum‑secure networks and satellite‑based quantum communication.
About BISAG‑N: An autonomous scientific society under MeitY, BISAG‑N works in space technology applications, satellite communication, geo‑informatics and supports technology‑driven governance.

sections.topic: Devaluation vs depreciation, appreciation vs revaluation
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Exchange rate systems and rupee movement; currency internationalisation › Devaluation vs depreciation, appreciation vs revaluation - meaning and trade effects
bullets: Depreciation: Regime Flexible/floating; What happens Exchange rate rises - more rupees per dollar; Done by Market demand-supply

Devaluation is an expenditure-switching policy: home goods become cheaper for foreigners and imports costlier at home, so spending switches to home-produced goods; it is a recognised method (with exchange depreciation, exchange control, monetary/fiscal measures, import curbs) to correct BoP disequilibrium.
Devaluation/depreciation makes exports cheaper (in foreign currency) and imports dearer, so the trade balance tends to improve - it does not raise export prices.
ES 2025-26: a weaker currency helps India's trade balance more than it hurts the financial channel (capital outflows); net impact positive.

Rupee: 5.4% depreciation in FY26 (to Jan), among the most depreciated with the yen (ES 2025-26); crossed 96.2/$ on 18-19 May 2026, down 6.3% since 1 Jan 2026, on Brent at $110.8 and FPI outflows (TH, 19 May 2026).

The scheme also provides for capacity augmentation of five NSTIs through National Centres of Excellence. Industry participation is incorporated through Strategic Investment Plans, Special Purpose Vehicles and Anchor Industry Partners.

Further, enrolment in ITIs across the country has increased from 9.51 lakh in the academic session 2014–15 to 14.70 lakh in the academic session 2025–26, indicating an increase of 54%.
Component I covers 1,000 Government ITIs , comprising 200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs .

items.title: NABKISAN Lists India’s First WASH-Focused Social Bond, Raises ₹180 Crore
items.summary: 03 OCT 2026 12:01PM by PIB Mumbai Mumbai, 3 October 2026 NABKISAN Finance Limited, a subsidiary of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), on 1st October 2026 listed India’s first Social Bond dedicated exclusively to the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) sector on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Mumbai.

facts.text: 03 OCT 2026 12:01PM by PIB Mumbai Mumbai, 3 October 2026 NABKISAN Finance Limited, a subsidiary of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), on 1st October 2026 listed India’s first Social Bond dedicated exclusively to the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) sector on the…
The Social Bond issue witnessed robust investor participation and was oversubscribed 1.8 times, enabling NABKISAN to raise ₹180 crore.
The five-year bond carries a coupon rate of 8.10%, matures in September 2031, and has been assigned the highest domestic credit ratings of CRISIL AAA (Stable) and CARE AAA (Stable).

The transaction was supported by a wide range of stakeholders, including Water.org as Technical Advisor and Knowledge Partner, along with market institutions, advisors, trustees and arrangers who contributed to the successful issuance and listing of the bond.

Composition: 7 (Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson (added by the 1995 amendment), 5 members); 5 including the Chairperson must be from minority communities (Section 3(2)); 3-year term; appointed by the Central Government, not the President.
Has civil-court powers while inquiring into complaints (LENSD, Jul 2026) (older notes say it has no automatic civil-court powers).

July 2026: Harjit Singh Grewal appointed Chairperson, filling a post vacant since April 2025 (after Iqbal Singh Lalpura); Munawari Begum Vice-Chairperson; Glenn E. Souza Ticlo member; now 4 of 7 posts filled (TH, 18 Jul 2026). The Delhi High Court had sought the Centre's reply on the vacancies (APPCA 2026).

sections.topic: M.M. Punchhi Commission (2007) · Recommendations on the Governor
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › M.M. Punchhi Commission (2007) - recommendations and their status › Recommendations on the Governor - tenure, removal and impeachment, role in universities
bullets: Delete "during the pleasure of the President" from Article 156. The Governor should be removed only by impeachment by the State Legislature, on the same lines as the President's impeachment.
Governors should not be made Chancellors of universities or given other statutory roles, so that the office stays out of day-to-day clashes with State governments.
Bills: a six-month deadline for the Governor to decide on bills passed by the Assembly, set by constitutional amendment. This repeats Sarkaria's call for a fixed time limit.
The Governor should not misuse discretionary powers. The nominee should be an eminent person who has not been in active politics, even at the local level, for a couple of years before appointment .
Exam angle: impeachment of the Governor, the 5-year tenure and the chancellor role are Punchhi's. Periodic "rotation of Governors" and "abolish the office" are distractors.

bullets: India's external debt: USD 718.2 billion at end-Dec 2024, 18.4% of GDP (ES 2025-26 Summary); external debt-GDP 20.4%, forex reserves cover 90% of it (RBI Annual Report, APPCA Jun 2026). India ranks 21st in the world, 11th in G20 (ES).

Most external debt is non-sovereign (owed by companies/banks); sovereign (government) external debt is small - the Government's external debt is about 2.6% of GDP and under 5% of its total debt (ES). Not all external debt is in US dollars (UPSC 2019: both statements wrong).
Sovereign external borrowing is mostly multilateral, concessional, project-linked; ADB is the largest multilateral lender (32.8%); then World Bank (IBRD/IDA), NDB, AIIB (CDI).
"India's External Debt: A Status Report" is published by the Ministry of Finance (DEA); RBI compiles the quarterly data .

bullets: Constituted 18 November 2004 (answer to "which year": 2004), chaired by Prof. M.S. Swaminathan; set up to address the calamity of farmer suicides; submitted five reports (2004-06) .
MSP formula: C2 + 50% (C2 = A2 + family labour + imputed rent/interest on owned land and capital); Government uses A2+FL x 1.5.
Core vision: farming should become economically viable and ecologically sustainable, and farmers' quality of life should improve (CDI).
Key recommendation: MSP = C2 + 50%. The government applies 50% over A2+FL instead (CDI).
Other recommendations: land reforms, irrigation, cheaper institutional credit, crop insurance and market reforms. The National Policy for Farmers, 2007 drew on its reports .

bullets: Critical Wildlife Habitat is defined in the FRA (UPSC 2018 key) - areas of national parks/sanctuaries to be kept inviolate, notified after an open process with affected communities .
Bamboo is a minor forest produce under FRA, with ownership vested in forest dwellers (UPSC 2019 key: statement 2 correct).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 22 › Forest and wildlife legal framework - Indian Forest Act 1927, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 › Protected area categories under the Act
bullets: Four PA types: sanctuary, national park, conservation reserve, community reserve (the last two added in 2002 ); tiger reserves are notified under the NTCA chapter.
NP: no rights, no grazing, boundary alteration only on NBWL recommendation. Conservation reserve: State-owned land near or linking PAs. Community reserve: private or community land, volunteered.
Network (2026, CDI): 109 NPs, 573 sanctuaries, 127 conservation reserves, 75 community reserves, 58 tiger reserves; over 1,000 PAs covering 5.32% of India (IYB).

bullets: CITES (1973): Mandate Regulate international wildlife trade; Legal status Legally binding on Parties, but does not replace national laws (APP)
CMS / Bonn Convention (1979): Mandate Conservation of migratory species (PYQ 2019); Legal status Binding treaty under UNEP
IUCN (1948): Mandate Red List/Red Data Book; runs thousands of field projects; Legal status Union of governments and NGOs, not a UN organ (APP; UPSC 2015 key: statements 2, 3)
TRAFFIC: Mandate Ensure wildlife trade is not a threat to conservation; Legal status NGO network of WWF and IUCN, not a UNEP bureau (UPSC 2017 key: 2 only)

bullets: Legal basis: Biosphere reserve UNESCO MAB recognition; no change in land's legal status or ownership; National park WPA 1972, state notification; Wildlife sanctuary WPA 1972, state notification
Human rights: Biosphere reserve Settlements allowed in transition zone; National park No rights, no grazing; Wildlife sanctuary Some rights; grazing regulated by Chief Wildlife Warden
Boundaries: Biosphere reserve Zoned core-buffer-transition; National park Clearly demarcated; Wildlife sanctuary Not strictly specified

Salary: the CEC and ECs are equal, on a par with a Supreme Court judge (APP). Service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage.

Action: refusal of Pullari, social boycott of officials at Macherla (even the Collector and SP); 300 cattle driven into the forest untaxed and impounded at Minchalapadu.

Leaders: Kanneganti Hanumanthu (killed in police firing at Minchalapadu, 26 Feb 1922; CDX misprints 2022); Congress men Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari studied and backed it; Konda Venkatappayya tried to dilute it (Congress had asked only for social boycott, not tax refusal).
Repression: 28 men and 8 women arrested; Unnava jailed (wrote the play *Nayakuralu* in jail); normalcy by March 1922.

sections.topic: Andhra Pradesh · Rain-shadow and drought-prone zone
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-2 › Andhra Pradesh - climate, rainfall regions, cyclone vulnerability, drought-prone areas › Rain-shadow and drought-prone zone
bullets: Rayalaseema lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats and the Karnataka/Telangana highlands, so it gets little SW-monsoon rain (CDI). Anantapur is the lowest-rainfall district.
Chronic droughts hit Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam when the NE monsoon fails; groundwater depletion adds to this (CDI).

2026: a deficient year. The SW monsoon deficit reached 51.2% (1 Jun-25 Aug), with all 28 districts deficient. Worst hit: Annamayya 75.9%, Prakasam 67.5%, Chittoor 65%. bullets: NPIT 2012: uses ICT as a driver of growth, jobs, governance reform and inclusion.
Twin goals: bring the full power of ICT within reach of the whole of India, and make India the Global Hub and Destination for IT and ITES Services by 2020.

Context: Indian IT was a USD 100 billion industry in 2011-12, 80% of revenue from exports; six hubs (Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, NCR) had ~90% of the industry and were near saturation, so the policy pushed IT into Tier II and Tier III cities.
Objectives: strengthen the global IT position; generate jobs; use ICT in education, health, skills, financial inclusion and governance; e-literacy for all.
The later Digital India, Aadhaar, UPI, BharatNet and DigiLocker are described as putting NPIT's vision into practice (CDI).

bullets: "Backward Classes" is not defined in the Constitution (APPSC G2 2017 key: the "defined" statement is the wrong one).

27% OBC quota in central jobs from 1993; in central educational institutions under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, in force Jan 2007 (IYB 2026 says 2007) after the 2005 amendment to Art. 15 (IYB) [GK for the Act's year].

sections.topic: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B) › Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .
105th Amendment, 2021 restored the States' power to prepare their own SEBC lists (after the Maratha quota judgment) .

bullets: Exit poll: a poll of voters taken immediately after they leave the polling station; not the same as an opinion poll (APPSC 2018 key: a, c, d correct).
Section 126A RPA 1951: no exit poll may be conducted or published from the start of polling in the first phase until half an hour after the close of the last phase .
Opinion polls are barred in the 48 hours before the close of poll (Sec. 126) .

bullets: Art. 243K (243ZA for municipalities): SEC appointed by the Governor, removable only like a High Court judge; service conditions cannot be varied to the SEC's disadvantage (APPCA, Apr 2026) [GK for last point].
Before 1993 states postponed local polls at will; the SEC and the 5-year term with elections before expiry (or within 6 months of dissolution, Arts. 243E/243U) made local government permanent (APP).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Impact of GST on commerce, industry and state finances; unresolved GST issues › Consuming vs producing states under destination-based tax
bullets: GST is a destination-based consumption tax: revenue goes to the State where goods/services are consumed, not produced.
IGST on inter-state supply (Art. 269A) is levied by the Centre and apportioned; the destination state gets the state share.
Effect: consuming states gain, manufacturing states (e.g., Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) feared loss - a key reason for the 5-year compensation guarantee .

Sunrise AP Vision 2029 (residual AP, after 2014): three staged goals: among the top three States by 2022 , the best State in India by 2029, and the most preferred global investment destination by 2050.
Exam angle: match the vision to its target year (2029 best State; 2050 investment destination; 2047 ₹308 lakh crore).

bullets: Art. 340: the President appoints a commission on socially and educationally backward classes (APP).
The Constitution does not define "backward classes" (G2 2017 key: that was the incorrect statement). Art. 16(4) backward classes are mainly identified by caste/social backwardness (Indra Sawhney).

Before 2018, Art. 338(10) treated references to SCs as including such backward classes as the President specified - hence BC complaints went to the SC commission ; the 102nd Amendment added Art. 366(26C) defining SEBCs by reference to Art. 342A .
National Backward Classes Commissions (Kaka Kalelkar, Mandal) → year + chairman
102nd Amendment (2018) gave the National Commission for Backward Classes constitutional status under Art. 338B [GK: amendment number].
